sources.title: Miguel A. Hernán and James M. Robins, Causal Inference: What If (2020; latest author revision 19 August 2026)
sources.locator: Full focused reading: Chapter 23 §§23.1–23.4 and Technical Points 23.1–23.3, printed pp. 323–331 (author PDF pp. 332–340). Extracted and inspected the complete focused pages, including the mediation-formula derivation, the NPSEM-IE/FFRCISTG distinction, the component-intervention story, and its limits.

contents.name: §23.1 and Technical Point 23.1: nested natural effects and mediation-formula factorization
§23.1 and Technical Point 23.1: cross-world independence is assumed under NPSEM-IE and not under FFRCISTG
§23.1 and §§23.2–23.3: mediator-outcome common causes, component interventions, and the limits of interpreting a natural effect as a feasible policy
contents.reason: The proof states the no-common-cause and no-treatment-induced-confounder premises; the separate target definition records the substantive component-intervention restrictions.

contents.name: Technical Point 23.2 and §23.4: separable interventionist effects and their component-specific targets
§23.3 and Fine Points 23.1–23.2: proposed separable-component stories can be empirically falsified by component trials
contents.reason: The definition makes component interventions and dismissible restrictions explicit and does not turn their scientific plausibility into a proved fact.

contents.name: Technical Point 23.3: front-door/path-specific identification under a distinct expanded graph
contents.reason: This is a separate front-door/path-specific target already assigned to the SCM/DAG supplier pair; it is not used to identify the natural effects here.

sources.title: Judea Pearl, Causal inference in statistics: An overview, §5.1 (Statistics Surveys 3, 2009)
sources.locator: Full focused reading of §5.1.1–§5.1.3, printed pp. 132–136 (author PDF pp. 37–41); the assigned natural-effect passage is §5.1.2–§5.1.3, printed pp. 134–136 / PDF pp. 39–41. The complete author PDF (52 pages according to the fetch stamp) was retrieved and inspected around the controlled, natural direct, and indirect definitions and the mediation formula.

contents.name: §5.1.1: controlled direct effects require intervention on the mediator; conditioning can open collider bias
§5.1.2: natural direct effect as a nested counterfactual and its sufficient unconfoundedness condition
§5.1.3: natural indirect effect, mediation functional, and total/direct/indirect algebra
§5.1.3 closing discussion: path-specific effects obtained by selecting paths rather than mediator values
contents.reason: General path-specific effects are broader than the single-mediator natural and separable targets commissioned in this pair; no such theorem is asserted here.
